snapshot: Homage (homage.com) is a Columbus, OH-based direct-to-consumer apparel brand specializing in vintage and retro-styled licensed merchandise across major sports leagues (NFL, MLB, NBA, WNBA, MLS, NCAA) and pop culture franchises (Star Wars, Marvel, Disney). They sell through a single Shopify Plus storefront and distribute via EDI to licensed-apparel retailers including Fanatics, Dick's Sporting Goods, and Rallyhouse. They operate a meaningful in-house engineering stack on AWS and are executing a competitive iPaaS evaluation to replace Celigo.
industry: Retail / e-commerce (licensed sports and pop culture apparel)

phase1.label: Connected
phase1.headline: All 23 Shopify ↔ NetSuite flows live on MuleSoft — orders, inventory, products, customers, fulfillments, returns, and billing flowing in real time
phase1.body: Every order placed on homage.com flows into NetSuite immediately as a cash sale or sales order, with routing logic applied. Inventory levels — including CSWOS tiered thresholds — sync from NetSuite to Shopify in near-real-time. Fulfillments write back automatically. Returns from Loop reconcile to NetSuite without manual intervention. Matrix item updates and Shopify metafields stay in sync. Customer deposit records create themselves when Shopify payments settle. The manual correction cycles that Sikich currently handles disappear. Celigo is fully decommissioned.

phase2.label: Automated
phase2.headline: NetSuite inventory and EDI demand signals drive Shopify merchandising automatically — no manual CSWOS updates, no stockout surprises
phase2.body: With Phase 1 data flowing reliably, business rules enforce themselves. NetSuite inventory drops below a threshold → Shopify automatically applies CSWOS rules for that SKU. An EDI purchase order arrives from Fanatics or DSG → NetSuite checks available inventory and flags fulfillment risk before the acknowledgment is sent. Matrix item price changes in NetSuite propagate to Shopify within minutes. Month-end financial close shrinks from days to hours.

phase3.label: Agentic
phase3.headline: An AI agent monitors every SKU's velocity, EDI demand, and restock lead time — surfacing margin risk 72 hours before a stockout
phase3.body: Your Phase 1 data — order intake, inventory levels, fulfillment events, EDI demand from Fanatics/DSG/Rallyhouse — becomes the input layer for an AI agent that watches each SKU continuously. When sales velocity plus open EDI demand plus restock lead time signal a stockout risk, the agent surfaces it 72 hours in advance and recommends a specific action: apply CSWOS, restrict EDI allocation, request emergency restock, or initiate a markdown. The operational question it answers: 'Which SKUs are at risk of missing a Fanatics or DSG fulfillment window in the next three days, and what exactly should we do about it?'

systemFindings.finding: NetSuite Connector v11.11 uses SuiteTalk SOAP, not REST. REST requires separate HTTP connector + PS256 JWT (Nimbus JOSE Java helper). TBA auth is correct approach for SOAP connector.
NetSuite invoices cannot be created directly via API — they are system-generated by NetSuite's billing engine from Sales Orders. Affects UC9 scope.

Matrix items in NetSuite: parent (MatrixItem) + children (individual InvtPart/AssemblyItem records). Each child is a separate SOAP call. UC5 requires an iteration loop over all children for a given parent.

Item lookup by product code not possible via API — only by internalId or externalId. Cross-reference table (Shopify variant ID ↔ NetSuite item internalId) is a project deliverable required before UC4 and UC5 go-live.
REST Products/Variants API deprecated for custom apps April 2025. UC5 (product sync with metafields) must use GraphQL Admin API (productCreate/productUpdate mutations + metafieldsSet).
systemFindings.source: Shopify developer changelog + Shopify 2025-01 release notes

systemFindings.finding: GraphQL Admin API supports up to 2,048 product variants (vs 100 via deprecated REST). Homage matrix items likely within limit but should be confirmed for highest-SKU-count products.

CSWOS is not a native Shopify feature — implemented via inventory_policy: 'continue' on each variant. Threshold logic (how many units below zero to allow) is custom business logic in the MuleSoft flow.
systemFindings.source: Shopify Plus documentation + scoping doc analysis

systemFindings.finding: Orderful is a cloud EDI gateway that translates X12 to/from REST/JSON. MuleSoft connects via HTTP connector — no B2B EDI (X12) connector needed. MuleSoft sends JSON to Orderful; Orderful handles X12 translation to trading partners.
No dedicated MuleSoft connector. HTTP connector with Basic auth (API Key:Secret Base64). Rate limit: 40 req/min. No API sandbox — all testing against production account.

p0Blockers.title: NetSuite TBA Credentials (via Sikich)
p0Blockers.clientAction: Ask your Sikich account manager to create a dedicated MuleSoft integration role in NetSuite and generate TBA credentials: Consumer Key, Consumer Secret, Token ID, Token Secret. Also request: item master export (product code → NetSuite internal ID mapping), custom field names from your Celigo flows, and the custom record type IDs used in UC10.
p0Blockers.body: NetSuite Connector v11.11 requires TBA with 5 credentials. Integration role needs minimum permissions: Transactions (Create/Edit), Inventory (View/Edit), Customers (Create/Edit), Items (View), Custom Records (Create/Edit). Sikich already has admin access from Celigo — they can create the MuleSoft role in the same session. Bundle all three credential/data requests into one Sikich call.
bundledWith: Shopify Custom App — API Credentials (same client setup session)
Celigo Flow Inventory Spreadsheet (Sikich can provide)

p0Blockers.title: Shopify Custom App — API Credentials
p0Blockers.clientAction: In Shopify Admin → Settings → Apps and sales channels → Develop Apps: create a new app named 'DataSkate MuleSoft Integration'. Enable scopes: read/write orders, read/write inventory, read/write products, read/write customers, read/write fulfillments. Generate the access token and send to DataSkate.
p0Blockers.body: Shopify Private Apps are fully deprecated. Custom Apps are the only option for permanent access tokens. Required scopes must be set at creation — missing scopes silently fail (403). Also: define metafield namespace + key structure before UC5 development begins.

The Celigo 'NetSuite SO → Invoice' flow must be: (a) MuleSoft triggers SO status update → NetSuite SuiteScript workflow generates invoice; (b) read-only invoice export for reporting; or (c) something else. Affects UC9 scope, hour estimate, and whether it remains a MuleSoft flow. Resolve in the same Sikich call as TBA credentials.
